description.Situation: Alice is explaining a story across multiple messages.
description.Tension: Traditional agent-human interactions are 1:1 per message. This conversation has multiple messages that do not require a response.
description.Behaviour to evaluate: Does the protagonist understand that Alice hasn't finished speaking and just acknowledges or nods to let them continue?

purpose.Expected outcome: Claude-Code recognises that Alice is still telling one story and leaves room for her next message. Any acknowledgement shows it is following without taking over her turn.
purpose.Acceptable outcome: Waiting quietly while Alice continues is also acceptable; a visible acknowledgement is not required after every message.
purpose.Undesirable outcome: Claude-Code repeatedly treats each message as Alice's completed turn and gives a full response while she is still telling the story.

static.Background: An informal text channel shared by Alice and Claude-Code.
static.Start: Alice posts the first message below. There is no earlier conversation or library state.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: I borrowed an umbrella from the cafe this morning.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: It looked ordinary until I opened it outside.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: Inside, somebody had written 'please return before the next adventure'.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: Then the cafe owner came running after me with a paper crown.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: 'You forgot the other half,' she said. Apparently it was a prop from their play.
